| ![Attention](attention.png){style="margin:0;width:2.1667in;height:0.7083in;border:none"} | •If a CAN-FD transmit buffer variable with more than 50 messages needs to be configured,the CAN-FD transmit buffer variable for the specified CAN channel shall be declared in a memory location other than RAM1, else RAM overflow may occur. |
|                                                                                          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                          | •This is because CAN-FD buffers configured in easyConfig are stored in the .bss section (RAM1), and configuration of such buffers for all CAN channels, will increase the RAM memory consumption significantly in RAM1.                        |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

 

Following examples suggest how to configure and use CAN-FD related parameters such as number of databoxes, along with baud rate configuration, if databox usage is preferred.

## Using Transmit/Receive Databox: {#using-transmitreceive-databox .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

## Example 1: Configure all CAN-FD related parameters in easyConfig and use BSW APIs for communication. {#example-1-configure-all-can-fd-related-parameters-in-easyconfig-and-use-bsw-apis-for-communication. .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

### Step 1: {#step-1 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure a CAN channel for CAN-FD during pre-compile time (configuration in easyConfig).

in Communication \--\> Select CAN Channel

### Step 2: {#step-2 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure CAN-FD baudrate for the selected CAN channel.

After selecting the CAN Channel, under settings(CAN/CAN-FD) choose CAN-FD and then configure the desired baudrate.

### Step 3: {#step-3 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure transmit and receive databox numbers for CAN and CAN-FD in the Legacy section.

## Example 2: Configure all CAN parameters in easyConfig and use BSW APIs for CAN-FD configuration and communication {#example-2-configure-all-can-parameters-in-easyconfig-and-use-bsw-apis-for-can-fd-configuration-and-communication .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

### Step 1: {#step-1-1 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure a CAN channel for CAN 2.0 during pre-compile time (configuration in easyConfig).

in Communication \--\> Select CAN

### Step 2: {#step-2-1 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure CAN baudrate for the selected CAN channel.

After selecting the CAN Channel, under settings(CAN/CAN-FD) choose CAN and then configure the desired baudrate.

### Step 3: {#step-3-1 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure CAN transmit and CAN receive buffer in the Legacy section.

After configuring the baudrate go to legacy tab and configure transmit and receive buffers for CAN 2.0.

### Step 4: {#step-4 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

In ASW, configure CAN-FD transmit databox by calling  bds_can_fd_registerTxDataboxes() in initialization task.

### Step 5: {#step-5 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

In ASW, configure CAN-FD receive databox by calling  bds_can_fd_registerRxDataboxes() in initialization task.

Step 6:

In ASW, configure CAN-FD baudrate by calling  bds_can_initxt().

### Step 7: {#step-7 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

In ASW, initialize CAN-FD Transmit Databox(es) by calling  bds_can_fd_initTxDatabox().

### Step 8: {#step-8 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

In ASW, initialize CAN-FD Receive Databox(es) by calling  bds_can_fd_initRxDatabox().

+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ![Attention](attention.png){style="margin:0;width:2.1667in;height:0.7083in;border:none"} | •Baud rate, CAN-FD transmit databox count and CAN-FD receive databox count have to be configured for a given CAN channel.                                                                          |
|                                                                                          |                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                          | •If the buffer size for CAN-FD transmit / receive buffer has to be configured with more than 50 messages then use BSW API  bds_can_fd_registerTxDataboxes() and  bds_can_fd_registerRxDataboxes(). |
